newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks hit all-time highs on rate cuts.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks hit all-time highs on rate cuts.

text.p: Toronto stocks hit all-time highs for a second straight session on Wednesday, powered by the Bank of Canada's decision to cut interest rates for the eighth time this year.
The TSE 300 Composite Index soared 58.48 points to close at 5388.03, surpassing the previous record set on Tuesday.
The key index also set a new intra-day peak of 5389.05.
Trading was brisk with volume of 110.04 million shares worth C$1.83 billion ($1.34 billion), the TSE's fifth-highest value ever.
Gold and bank stocks led the charge which resulted in 10 of 14 sub-groups finishing higher.

Canada's central bank cut its key bank rate by a quarter of a percentage point to 4.0 percent. The move prompted major banks to drop their prime lending rates to 5.5 percent from 5.75, their lowest level since February 1994.
Bank stocks rallied on the rate cuts with three of six major banks reaching 52-week highs.
The gold group added 244 points on rising gold prices. COMEX December gold ended up US$1.30 an ounce at US$382.30, but gold traders said the market's recent downtrend is intact.
Toronto's advancing stocks outnumbered declines 532 to 400 with 285 issues ending flat.
* Bank of Nova Scotia was the top bank stock by volume, closing up 0.70 at 39.70 on 2.5 million shares.
Royal Bank of Canada climbed 1.05 to 40.60, a 52-week high. Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce rose 1 to end at 51.30 after earlier hitting a 52-week peak of 51.40.
* Among gold stocks, Barrick Gold Corp. gained 1.25 to 36.50 on 1.8 million shares. Barrick said earlier it increased reserves at its Pascua mine in Chile by 18 percent.
* Takeover target Loewen Group Inc. sank 1.30 to 56 on profit-taking as traders predicted a long fight with hostile bidder Service Corp. International.
